title: Eight months ago Altman wanted an AI CEO. Now he says nobody does.
excerpt: In November, Sam Altman wanted OpenAI to be the first big company run by an AI boss. He said it would be an embarrassment if it were not. This week, he said people do not want an AI boss at all. “Shame on me if OpenAI is not the first big company run by an […]
content_html:
In November, Sam Altman wanted OpenAI to be the first big company run by an AI boss. He said it would be an embarrassment if it were not. This week, he said people do not want an AI boss at all.

“Shame on me if OpenAI is not the first big company run by an AI CEO,” he said on the Conversations with Tyler podcast last year. He framed being beaten to it as a failure.

Eight months later, on the Invest Like the Best podcast, he took the opposite view, Business Insider reported. The OpenAI boss now says the market wants a human in the chair.

“The world wants to know about the person that’s going to be responsible for the decisions of a company,” Altman said. “And they don’t really want an AI CEO.”

A pattern of walking it back

The 💜 of EU tech

The latest rumblings from the EU tech scene, a story from our wise ol' founder Boris, and some questionable AI art. It's free, every week, in your inbox. Sign up now!

The reversal fits a habit. Altman has spent the past year softening the maximalist predictions that made his name.

He once warned that AI would wipe out “entire classes” of jobs. He now says he is delighted to be wrong about the short-term hit to entry-level work. It is part of a wider narrative flip. The bosses who warned AI would take your job now insist it will not.

His explanation is that people still prefer people. “I definitely would much rather engage with a person than engage with an AI for almost everything,” he said. He pointed to art. “You read a novel, you want to know about the person behind it.”

Conviction or convenience

There is an obvious tension. Altman sells the most aggressive vision of AI in the industry. A message that humans remain irreplaceable suits him. His tools take the blame for cutting jobs and flooding feeds with machine-made content.

He does gesture at something real. AI can now do much of what people do. It still stumbles on the judgment a good manager or artist brings. Altman admits the industry lacks the vocabulary for it.

“The world may need a new kind of word for the kind of judgment that people are very good at, that AIs seem to really deeply struggle with,” he said.

It is a striking thing to concede. This is the man who recently wanted to hand his own job to a machine. Whether the humans keep the corner office, or Altman changes his mind again, is the open question.

content_html_zh:
11 月，Sam Altman 希望 OpenAI 成为第一家由 AI 老板经营的大公司。 他说，如果不这样做，那就太尴尬了。 本周，他表示人们根本不想要人工智能老板。

“如果 OpenAI 不是第一家由人工智能首席执行官运营的大公司，我会感到羞耻，”他去年在与泰勒对话播客中说道。 他认为被打败是一种失败。

据《商业内幕》报道，八个月后，他在《Invest Like the Best》播客中提出了相反的观点。 OpenAI 的老板现在表示，市场需要一个人坐在椅子上。

“全世界都想知道谁将负责公司的决策，”奥特曼说。 “而且他们并不真正想要一位人工智能首席执行官。”

这种逆转符合一种习惯。 奥特曼在过去的一年里软化了他成名的极端主义预测。

他曾警告说，人工智能将消灭“所有类别”的工作岗位。 他现在表示，他很高兴自己对入门级工作的短期打击的看法是错误的。 这是更广泛的叙事翻转的一部分。 那些警告人工智能会抢走你工作的老板们现在坚称它不会。

他的解释是，人们还是更喜欢人。 “我肯定更愿意与人打交道，而不是在几乎所有事情上与人工智能打交道，”他说。 他指的是艺术。 “你读一本小说，你想了解小说背后的人物。”

信念或方便

有一种明显的紧张感。 Altman 推销的是业内最激进的人工智能愿景。 人类仍然不可替代的信息很适合他。 他的工具因削减工作岗位和充斥机器制作的内容而受到指责。

他确实对着一些真实的东西做了手势。 人工智能现在可以做人类做的很多事情。 它仍然会受到优秀经理或艺术家的判断的影响。 奥特曼承认该行业缺乏相关词汇。

他说：“世界可能需要一种新的词语来形容人们非常擅长的判断，而人工智能似乎确实在与之深深挣扎。”

承认这一点是一件令人震惊的事情。 这个人最近想把自己的工作交给机器。 到底是人类保住角落办公室，还是奥特曼再次改变主意，这是一个悬而未决的问题。
